findings.title: Receiving request socket is destroyed immediately after writing the 413 body, so the client may never see the 413
findings.evidence: In the over-limit path the handler does 'res.status(413).json({ error: ... })' and on the very next line calls 'req.destroy();'. The 413 body is written to the socket asynchronously, while IncomingMessage._destroy marks the message aborted (it is incomplete, since reading stopped mid-body) and tears down the socket, dropping pending writes.
findings.recommendation: Flush the response first, then close the connection: e.g. write the 413, set Connection: close, and destroy the socket/request from a res 'finish'/'close' handler (res.on('finish', () => req.destroy())) or stop consuming with req.pause() and let the response complete. Add a test that an oversized body yields status 413 rather than ECONNRESET.

findings.title: Parsed value is assigned to req.body without requiring an object, so a body of null/scalar/array violates the object contract downstream
findings.evidence: The parser does 'req.body = JSON.parse(text);' for any valid JSON. A request with Content-Type: application/json and body 'null' takes the success path and leaves req.body === null (same for '42', '"x"', '[]'), so any handler reading a property of req.body throws TypeError and returns 500 instead of a 4xx client error.
findings.recommendation: After parsing, reject non-object results (typeof parsed !== 'object' || parsed === null || Array.isArray(parsed)) with 400, matching strict JSON-body semantics, or document and test the intended contract for top-level arrays/scalars.

findings.title: Byte accounting assumes Buffer chunks; if an earlier middleware set request encoding the cap is under-counted and Buffer.concat throws
findings.evidence: The comment asserts byte semantics via 'received += chunk.length;', but chunk.length is only bytes while chunks are Buffers. If any upstream middleware calls req.setEncoding('utf8'), chunk.length counts UTF-16 code units, so a multi-byte body can exceed MAX_BODY_BYTES without tripping the cap, and line 27's Buffer.concat(chunks) throws TypeError on string chunks (unhandled 500).
findings.evidence_quote: received += chunk.length; // Buffer length: bytes, not characters
findings.recommendation: Coerce defensively: use Buffer.byteLength(chunk) when a chunk is a string, and Buffer.from(chunk) before pushing, or explicitly document/enforce that this middleware must run before any setEncoding call. Add a test with a multi-byte UTF-8 body near the cap.

findings.title: Empty or whitespace-only body is silently accepted as an empty object
findings.evidence: The end handler short-circuits with 'req.body = {};' and next() when text.trim() === '', so a client that sends Content-Type: application/json with no body gets a success path instead of a 400. For a strict JSON parser this hides client bugs and differs from strict body-parser behaviour (which 400s on an empty body).
findings.recommendation: Decide the contract explicitly: return 400 for an empty/whitespace body, or keep the {} default and document plus test it so downstream handlers can rely on it.
